distinguishing_features: Actively diverts flow to shift operating point away from cavitation-prone regime using Direct Transfer (TRIZ P5) of potential energy
Prevents low-pressure condition rather than detecting or mitigating it
Maintains runner in high-load, high-pressure regime or shuts down to zero-flow until safe operation
Enforces minimum cavitation number via flow coefficient control through real-time calculation and valve actuation
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to prevent cavitation erosion on hydro turbine runner blades at part load without modifying runner geometry or relying on post-onset detection
parsed.viable_reason: The mechanism uses standard components and established fluid dynamics principles to enforce a safe operating envelope, which is physically realizable at scale.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The approach shifts from detection or geometric adaptation to proactive flow diversion based on cavitation physics, which is not a routine extension of existing monitoring or design practices.
